needs: A sequence over time: messages cross between two timelines in a fixed order.

brief.title: The TCP three-way handshake
brief.idea: Before any data flows, TCP opens a connection with three messages, SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK, so both sides agree on the numbers their bytes start from.

beats.say: A laptop wants a page from a server. Before any data moves, T C P opens a connection.
beats.show: Two vertical lines appear, the laptop on the left and the server on the right, with time running downward.

beats.say: It takes three messages, and along the way each side picks a starting number for counting its bytes.
beats.show: Three empty arrow slots appear between the two lines, stacked downward in time.

beats.say: First the client sends S Y N, which says, let us talk, and my bytes start at one thousand.
beats.show: An arrow labelled SYN, seq 1000 travels down and across from the client to the server.

beats.say: The server answers S Y N A C K. It acknowledges one thousand and one, and its own bytes start at five thousand.
beats.show: An arrow labelled SYN-ACK travels back from the server to the client, lower on the timeline.

beats.say: Last, the client sends A C K, acknowledging five thousand and one. Both sides now agree.
beats.show: A third arrow labelled ACK travels from the client to the server, lower still.

beats.say: If one trip across takes twenty milliseconds, the client waits forty before it can send its request.
beats.show: A bracket on the client line spans from the SYN leaving to the SYN-ACK arriving, labelled 40 ms.

beats.say: A server on the far side of the world, a hundred and fifty milliseconds away, makes the client wait three hundred.
beats.show: A second, longer pair of timelines shows a distant server, with its bracket labelled 300 ms.

beats.say: Then the request goes out right behind the final A C K, and the page starts to flow back.
beats.show: A fourth arrow labelled GET follows just below the ACK, then a thicker arrow of data returns.

beats.say: Three messages: S Y N, S Y N A C K, and A C K.
beats.show: The three arrows are highlighted one after another on the two timelines.

beats.say: Each one carries a number, so both sides know exactly where the bytes of the other begin.
beats.show: The numbers 1000 and 5000 are circled on the arrows that first carried them.
